Job Market Index · Switzerland · German-speaking Switzerland

Job Market Index — German-speaking Switzerland

Weekly snapshot of German-language job postings across 3 platforms in Switzerland (jobs.ch, arbeit.swiss, jobscout24.ch). Latest snapshot: 2026-09-05. Counts are what each platform publicly reports for the tracked search terms. We measure ads written in German — a German-language posting in a company outside the Deutschschweiz is included; we do not filter by canton. French, Italian-language sections coming next.

By industry — German-language job postings in Switzerland

Each bar is one Swiss job platform’s current open-position count in that industry. jobs.ch uses its native Branche filter; arbeit.swiss and jobscout24.ch (no native industry filter) are aggregated from their occupation data via canonical mapping — see methodology below.

By occupation — German-language job postings in Switzerland

Top 12 job titles per industry, based on real search-query counts across all 3 Swiss platforms. Titles were selected by pilot-testing ~115 candidate terms per industry and keeping the highest-signal twelve (deduped for gender variants and qualification suffixes). Bars platform-colored for direct comparison.

Every industry below is scrapeable from jobs.ch · arbeit.swiss · jobscout24.ch — pay per result, no monthly fee.

2062 observations across 2 snapshot(s), 3 platform(s). CC BY 4.0. Cite as "NanoScrape Job Market Index, 2026-09-05".

Methodology

  • What is measured: job postings visible on a given platform on a given date. Not vacancies, not hires.
  • Counts are what the platform reports, not our own count. Where they differ, we publish the measured deviation.
  • Platform figures are not comparable and are not summed. The same position appears on multiple boards; combined totals would double-count.
  • arbeit.swiss is a public employment service subject to the Swiss Stellenmeldepflicht, which mandates reporting of vacancies in occupations with above-average unemployment. Its occupational composition is systematically different from commercial boards and is not a market-share proxy.
  • Keyword set is derived from ESCO / ISCO-08 and frozen per taxonomy version. Any change ships as a new version and both run in parallel for at least three months so the series can be spliced.
  • Sampling: weekly, Tuesday 06:00 UTC. Job posting volume has a strong weekday cycle; a fixed weekday removes that.
  • Revision policy: published figures are never silently edited. Corrections appear as a dated revision note.
